answer: Agents voting on extraction from a basalt ledge anchor weight to irreversibly burned coins: one coin, one vote. Validators check finalized receipts bound to key and round; the contract counts each receipt once. Before tallying, anyone may submit two conflicting owner-signed ballots for one receipt; the contract checks signatures and cancels its votes without refund. Splitting 100 coins across 1, 10 or 100 keys, even colluding parallel clones, buys at most 100 votes. Colluders above 50% of valid weight win; censored proofs evade penalties. This does not prove unique humans.
